text_fidelity_a:
Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold I work in live AV production, and usually keep a pair of Sony over-the-ear headphones in my gear bag for monitoring sound on location. Quality of the sound is important for concert and other live music gigs. But those big Sonys take up a lot of space, so I've been considering a good set of IEMs for a while now. In the past I haven't had good results from anything that wasn't a large over-the-ear set, and I have small ears that reject a lot of ear-bud style devices so I was excited to get a chance to try these out.

Ok, to be fair, I don't have any other IEMs to compare this to, but I'm BLOWN AWAY at how incredible they sound at such a miniscule size. I put on the smallest tips for my ears and they actually stay in relatively well, and create the passive noise cancellation I was expecting but without being uncomfortable to wear for an extended period of time. But the range of sound reproduced was something I have only experienced in larger studio headphones!
A perk of IEMs versus larger headphones on jobs like mine are that I can pull out one so I can hear the sound around me while monitoring with my other ear (great if working with an audio engineer who needs to communicate with me on the job), and it comes with a pretty nifty case to wrap it up and slide into my bag. The case makes it bigger than it needs to be, but honestly this is so much less space than my old headphones took up, and keeps the cord from getting tangled. I love it!
For personal use, they sound great even on consumer equipment, but they really shine on devices that can drive the additional range such as my old LG V20 with it's Quad DAC built in (one of the reasons I keep that old device around!).
The price tag is a little steep for me personally, but my Sony headphones retail somewhere around this (I had bought them used), and I KNOW there are pricier options out there, so it seems to fit right into the audiophile equipment range.
text_fidelity_b: Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold

text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung I ordered the 'Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts after a few weeks.

First off, this thing is actually pretty amazing. The build quality is nice and aesthetically it looks clean. The sound quality is nice but not phenomenal. However for how small it is, it does produce decent sound and for a bedside alarm clock it does quite well. The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. The fast charger also works with my wireless earbuds which I attached an image showing the charge light on the Wakey, and the wireless earbuds case indicating charging. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra EASYGO Bluetooth Headset [Retail Packaging] As a general rule, I hate hands-free handsets.

I hate it when I begin speaking with someone, and I think they're agreeing with everything I say, and then it turns out they're actually talking to someone else using their dratted ear extension with the flashing blue light.

I hate the fact that my ears are the wrong size and shape for the majority of headsets.

I hate it when my untrained (clumsy) fingers hit the wrong part of the headset when I'm simply trying to stop it from falling to its death from a height of just over 5 feet, and I either redial the last number or hang up on the one person who hates being hung up on.

Plus, they're UGLY, and don't accessorise well with any wardrobe!!

HOWEVER,

I hate it even more when I have to pull over and park to take or make a call.

And I especially hate it if I DON'T pull over, and then get busted by the only policeman on the entire empty highway who has insomnia and a full book of blank tickets waiting to be filled in.

SO,

Hands free it shall be -
But ONLY when I'm driving.

That said, this device fits most of my basic needs, and throws in some convenient extras. The EASYGO Headset was indeed very easy to set up and even easier to use. Sound quality was good and the spoken connection status and audio volume adjuster are useful features.

The headset is also relatively small and stylish (as hands-free headsets go) without any flashing lights or buttons that attract unwanted attention (or cause an attack of photosensitive epilepsy, or signal the letters N-E-R-D in morse code.)

The most impressive feature of this headset has to be the long battery life, which is great because the miserly charger cord is so awkward to use that you don't want to have to use it more often than necessary. Besides, as I only use it in the car, it lasts me several trips, depending on how often and how long I prattle.

Admittedly it is more comfortable to use than I expected. The extra ear hook prevents suicidal leaps from ear to earth, and it doesn't weigh my head down on one side.

In summary, for a simple headset, it delivers.

Rated: 4.5 stars

Amanda Richards
January 19, 2011
text_fidelity_b: Jabra EASYGO Bluetooth Headset [Retail Packaging]

Otium Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.0 Headphones with Digital Intelligence LED Display 3500 mAH Charging Case 135H Playtime Stereo Sound Headset IPX8 Waterproof Built-in Mic for Home Office… Great ear buds, and they arrived super quickly as well!

The ear buds come with a charging case, usb charging cord, several size ear pieces, and the ear buds themselves.
The charging case comes almost all the way charged, mine was at 98% upon delivery, and the ear buds were also fairly well charged at about 80%. They're held in the case with magnets, which is nice for storage and piece of mind, knowing they will stay put while charging. The charging case can actually be used as a power bank for your phone/mobile device too, which is pretty awesome! I didn't realize this at purchase, so it was a nice bonus.

After fully charging both for first time use, the buds will auto pair with each other when taken off the charging case. They paired very easily with my galaxy s9, and I was actually pleasantly surprised by the sound quality.
They touch sensitive area on the ear buds is most of the outer area shown when put into your ear, so be sure to get the situated first, and then turn your music on to avoid awkward on/off mishaps while putting them on.

The instructions included are very clear. Left ear is long hold volume down, right is long hold volume up, skipping tracks back or forward is quick press of either ear. Answering and ending calls can be done from either ear also.
These can also be used in single ear mode (using the left as the "master" pod), and will auto switch to the right pod as master if the left dies, so you can continue single ear use while charging the left.

Overall these are very nice little ear pods for a great price. If you are shopping around, I absolutely recommend buying these!

It looked perfect for my oldest son who is a huge 80's music fan and thought he should hear it in its original format. We were excited to unbox it and play the two albums we picked up at the used book store. First impressions were OK. The case looks nice and love the two speakers built in. Opening it, we were underwhelmed by the plastic turntable, stylus arm and rather cheap looking controls. But we were still excited.

The sound was also a little disappointing. The two speakers are underpowered and all high end so it was pretty tinny. But the absolute worst was that they stylus is so head light that it skipped constantly. We put a small glass bead on it and the weight actually slowed the turntable. We backed off and placed a quarter on it and it played about right. But again, I was underwhelmed by the underpowered turntable. Also, we noted that one of the spongy pads on the turn table was not installed properly and put a list to the album. We fixed that and fixed the quarter to the stylus and we were able to get it to play through Adam Ant's Friend or Foe album. The scratchy quality of between songs brought me back 40 years to my own first phonograph, which I think was pretty crappy, but probably better than this one.

It works, its nostalgic. We have had fun and will probably get an album at every used bookstore, garage sale, or antique store we find them in, but we will need to upgrade if he goes beyond just enjoying the novelty of it.

text_fidelity_a:
JAM XT Extreme Wireless Speaker, Splash Proof, Drop Proof, Dirt Proof IP64 Rating, Carabiner Clip, Built-in Speakerphone, Works with iPhone, Android, Bluetooth Devices, HXP430BK Black I will give you the down and dirty in short bullet form. Hopefully this answers most questions.

PROS of this product
* Easy to set up and use.
* Quality of the sound is good and it isn't heavy on the bass. Music is clear. The one speaker (mono) gives off great sound.
*Item is portable and sturdy.
*Item has Bluetooth function or you can hook it straight to your device. (I used my son's cord from his VModa head-set to connect to my android. ) Otherwise I used the Bluetooth function on my IPAD, IPOD and Nexus 4 (android phone) with no problem. The range or reception is decent. I didn't have any breaks in the connection, but I really didn't try to go too far. I tend to stay in the same room or in the general area, while listening to music.
*You can control the sound from your device or from the speaker. AND you can still pause your music using your device.
*Easy to charge. I really liked the fact that it is compatible with any USB or android charger. Meaning if you have an Apple device (ex., IPOD or IPAD), etc you can use the charger to charge this speaker. Or at least use the base portion of the charger. If you have an android, you can use that cord as well. The charge life for the battery is reasonable, and it even comes with a lithium battery.
*You can attach it to a book-bag or backpack (as shown in the photo), but I just place it where I want it to be and put it down. It is small enough (about the size of the palm of my hand) to fit into any purse, or bag without making it too heavy. Basically you can use this anywhere (in the home, camping, on trips, at the beach) and at any time.
* It's cute (I have the black. It kind of looks like a smashed soda can). Again, it's small. There are controls and indicator lights on the bottom of the device. The charge area is located on the top.
*Price seems comparable with other products of this sort (wireless speakers) on the market.

THINGS I WOULD CHANGE (not really a CON) about this product:
*The USB cord could be a bit longer. It was a little short for my tastes. But at least it's versatile.

So, as you can see, I was pleased with this product. The PROS definitely outweigh the "things that I would change" category. It had everything that made this a winner. It was easy to set up, and has decent sound quality. I definitely would recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: JAM XT Extreme Wireless Speaker, Splash Proof, Drop Proof, Dirt Proof IP64 Rating, Carabiner Clip, Built-in Speakerphone, Works with iPhone, Android, Bluetooth Devices, HXP430BK Black

I actually cracked the case open using a credit card and extracted the drive to put inside my tower (currently have 3 drives in there, and was replacing one).
You may be wondering why I chose this over an internal drive if that's all I wanted. Well, there are 2 reasons:
1) This is actually less expensive than a bare drive for some reason
2) You get a free external enclosure thrown in!

After removing the drive and cloning my old one to this one with Acronis software, I took the old drive and put it back inside of this enclosure. Great, now not only did I expand my internal 2GB to 4, but I now have a nifty 2GB external for backups and moving data physically. All for less money than an internal drive would have cost. Win win!

NOTE: This will almost definitely void the warranty, if that sort of thing is a concern to you.

BN-LINK Smart Power Strip Compatible with Alexa Google Home, Smart Plug WiFi Outlets Surge Protector with 4 USB 3 Charging Port Multi Plug Extender,15A This is a very good quality smart surge protector. It has a great mix of features for the price.

Pluses
1. Outlets are widely spaced for large wall "wart" power adapters
2. Smart outlets can be remotely controlled through the app (iOS & Android)
3. Voice assistant compatible
4. USB-A ports allow for additional device charging
5. No "hub" required to use remotely

Minuses
1. Only 6 outlets
2. 2.4 GHz Wi-FI means you need to enable the 2.4 GHz radio on your Wi-Fi router/access point in order to connect to the surge protector remotely
3. USB ports only go up to 5 amps (no fast charging)
4. Only rated to 600 joules, on the low end of surge protection

You can use this surge protector without enabling the smart capabilities. However, once you download the app to your device and connect to the 2.4 GHz radio of your Wi-Fi router/access point, pairing to the device
is pretty straightforward. Using the app is easy and allows for some pretty cool programmming, such as timers to turn on & off the outlets. I haven't tried out the voice assistant capabilities, but I'm assuming they work
as intended.

ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa I'm not a gamer, but I do have around 30 devices connected to a home network. These include WEMO switches, Amazon Echos, a smart TV, a playstation, Kindles, iPads, printers, and smartphones. The "dynamic Quality of Service" feature of this NIGHTHAWK X4 ULTIMATE GAMING ROUTER (R7500v2) seems to prioritize these devices, so that all of them are more responsive (faster connections) than they were with my previous router (a rock-solid NIGHTHAWK (R7000)).

When this NIGHTHAWK (R7500v2) is set up, it recognizes all of the "Internet of things" devices for what they are. In the "attached devices" list, these aren't given device names (e.g., "iPad", picked up from the device itself) but have "n/a" in the name column (and you can't assign them names even if you know them by the MAC numbers). I don't know exactly how the "Quality of Service" feature performs its magic, but now when I ask an Amazon Echo to turn on a light or a fan, the Echo performs the task immediately--instead of with a delay while it searched through the router's list of connected devices for the correct one.

The PCs and other devices that use lots of bandwidth (instead of being on standby much of the time) seem to connect faster, and they test (using OOKLA) at significantly faster Internet speeds.

My R7500v2 is broadcasting signals for both bands (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), and my compatible devices connect with the 5 GHz network whenever I ask them to. However, I don't use the 5 GHz band for anything at present (because it's easiest to have everything that uses a printer on the same band with the printers). Thus I don't know whether the router frequently drops the 5 GHz signal, as other reviewers have stated.

I've used several high-end Linksys routers, and they have performed very well. However, I find that Netgear routers lose their Internet signal far less often, and almost never require rebooting--when Netgear routers need rebooting, the issue is almost always traceable to Comcast problems.

Another reason that I prefer Netgear routers over Linksys routers is that Netgear has no limit (or a very high limit) on the number of devices that you can list by MAC number and tell the router to "allow only these devices to connect to the network". I use this feature as an extra firewall, and find that the Linksys 25-device list is inadequate for my needs.

Finally, the Netgear "Genie" app for managing the router settings is clear and easy to understand. The initial setup for this router is easy, unless you have a nonstandard home network (e.g., my router is connected with the Comcast-supplied equipment in "Bridge" mode), and/or you interrupt the setup routine before it's run through all its steps. If you do land in setup limbo, you can start over by resetting the router to the factory settings (use a paperclip to hold down the reset button for 10-30 seconds--light will blink; unplug from wall for 30 seconds; follow Quick Start instructions again from beginning).
text_fidelity_b: Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
GorillaPod Video Tripod (Black/Blue) The Gorillapod Video Tripod (Black/Blue) is a good idea on paper but in real life it just doesn't quite measure up.

The pan & tilt head is incredibly stiff which leads to jerky motion and bounce in your video. There also, on mine at least, appears to be a good bit of free play or slack in the vertical movement of the control arm. I've tried to tighten this down to no avail. The mounting screw seems to be a bit long. It wasn't bad mounting my RCA Small Wonder video camera but when I mounted my Kodak still camera the screw bottomed out and left the camera loose on the mount. The mount itself seems quite secure tight and sturdily attached to the tripod.

I like the adjustability of the legs but if you're not using the tripod on a metal surface for the magnetic feet to cling to it tends to just slide around when adjusting the pan or tilt. The magnets do appear to be strong for their size and will hold my RCA Small Wonder video camera fully horizontal on the 'fridge or door of my car. I tried this with my Kodak Z-650 still camera and it was too heavy for the magnets to support.

While on the subject of the magnetic feet I wanted to add a warning that if you're using an older CRT style monitor care should be taken to keep this tripod several feet away from your monitor. Even being more than a foot away from my 19" CRT cause distortion and image warping. There is the potential for damage to CRT monitors.

As a stationary camera mount this is a pretty cute product; easy to carry, lightweight with near infinitely adjustable legs. If you just want to plop down your camera so you don't have to hold it this product works fine. When you bring the flaws of the pan and tilt features into play the enjoyment goes downhill fast.

All in all it's not bad but it really isn't great.
text_fidelity_b: GorillaPod Video Tripod (Black/Blue)

Now the bad stuff. I started trying to set this thing up nearly 8 hours ago. You have to download a smartphone app from your apple or google play store. Once you open it, be prepared to provide every media related password in your entire universe ...which won't be easy because the Chromecast interface is TERRIBLE. The main reason I bought the thing was that I hope to add HBOMax to my lineup, since it went away on Roku. I still have no idea how to do that, since I have so far not found any options by which to search for HBOMax from within the Chromecast interface to download or select it as an option. I've tried to add my Pandora account, which login info works just fine on my laptop and smartphone, but the Chromecast interface rejects it as incorrect.

Still in the process of setup, but I will update later once I've figured this poorly designed mess out...

text_fidelity_a:
Haier L32A2120 32-Inch 720p 60Hz LCD HDTV I scored this TV on the black Friday gold box deal and I have to admit I really wasn't sure how the quality of this tv would be. I ordered this for an extra bedroom and thought for the price it would work.

The good:
- The TV was well packaged and protected and Amazon had it to my door a few days after I ordered it
- Nothing was missing from the box
- When my wall mount kit came in after a few mods to the kit ( nothing to do with the TV ) I had it on the wall and up and running with no issues and the TV turned on to the setup wizard.
- The TV was directly connected to cable without a box, auto scan found a bunch of channels and bang TV was ready
- The TV is not to heavy
- The ports are at the bottom of the TV and easy access
- The Remote is OK, not to high tech but not to generic looking and works well
- The picture was great and it's viewing angles no issues - Very clean picture I have to say

The Not so Good:
- The TV thickness is is between thin and thick ( so for wall mounting it stick out a tad )
- The TV power cable has to have a little bit of a bend in it ( no big deal )
- The frame / Plastic is OK, but not as heavy duty feeling as your used to with higher end TV's
- Channel numbers are not standard or maybe I am missing something... I get stations like 2.0, 2.1, 3.0 so on

Over All:
- I was very impressed by the picture quality and general quality of the tv and for the black Friday price it was a Killer deal. If you looking for a extra tv set for the bedrooms, or family room this is a perfect low cost set with a great picture. Thanks Amazon
text_fidelity_b: Haier L32A2120 32-Inch 720p 60Hz LCD HDTV

text_fidelity_a:
Fit & Fresh Protective Laptop Sleeve with Zippered Storage Pocket, Laptop Bag fits Apple/Microsoft/Acer/Samsung/Google/Lenovo with up to 15.6" Displays, Space Dyed, Gray I have a wonderful hybrid laptop/tablet but the problem is that I needed a case that was slim, but would protect my laptop even while it was being charged. I had a few dings in it from banging on edges of things, so when I saw this, I was hoping it would be perfect. Let's see what happened..

WHAT IS THIS SLEEVE LIKE?
I have backpacks, and big cases to put laptops in, but I just wanted a protective sleeve. That is precisely what this is. It is a fabulous protective sleeve for protecting the laptop. It is lined in very soft velveteen. There is a zipper pocket on the front which has a metal zipper, but is lined with BRIGHT LIME GREEN LINING. I am sorry. I had to capitalize that because I am so excited about it. It is slick so anything put inside will slide in and out easily. It matches the small colored patch on either end of the sleeve.

The outside of the sleeve is like dark denim in color. It is tougher than denim, however. The inside is a light gray. All edges are bound in tough nylon so there are no edges to fray. Workmanship is excellent on this. It is well made.

DOES IT FIT?
My laptop is a 15inch laptop and it fits perfectly. The most exciting part is that I can leave it unzipped and it gives me the room to leave the recharging jack in the laptop so I can recharge it while protecting it. When not recharging, I can zip it shut, put the charger in the pocket and be on my way. I can also zip from both sides leaving the top open if I want and the cord can still come out for recharging. (It has a two way zipper with two zipper heads on each end).

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a protective sleeve that is fresh looking and protective, this is a winner for me. It is soft inside, bright lined outside pocket, and strong workmanship all around. I am very happy with this and highly recommend it.

MY RATING
Five stars for this.
text_fidelity_b: Fit & Fresh Protective Laptop Sleeve with Zippered Storage Pocket, Laptop Bag fits Apple/Microsoft/Acer/Samsung/Google/Lenovo with up to 15.6" Displays, Space Dyed, Gray

Bose Smart Soundbar 900 Dolby Atmos with Alexa Built-In, Bluetooth connectivity - White I researched soundbars on youtube and written reviews on just about every site I could find on all soundbars. Hours upon hours. Everything kept leading me back to the Bose 900. I was a little hesitant with reviews that mentioned how hard it was to set up and the app not working well. I'll just say I had zero issues with any of this. From taking it out of the box and setting it up , everything went seamlessly. Now maybe I got really lucky, but again, zero issues.

As far as the sound, it is exactly what I was wanting and more. I was concerned about my ceiling height which is angled and 12ft high at the highest point. I'll just say watching Dune exceeded my expectations. I heard sounds all the way around me. Maybe Im also lucky with my room set up, but it performed better than i expected.

I am using the soundbar by itself with no additional sub or surround speakers. The soundbar gives me more than enough bass and as far as surround im more than impressed. The dialogue is exactly what i wanted, etc.

I highly recommend the calibration from the get go. I never bothered with the standard settings and just did the calibration from the start.

All in all this thing met all the requirements. I may get the Bose 700 surround as extra enhancement, but I still feel its not fully needed. The Bose 900 does it all in my case.

One other thing is that some content might not sound the same, which is normal for any set up, but adjusting the settings from the app couldnt be anymore easier and i dont feel its a complaint. I guess if taking a minute to adjust a movie bothers you, well then so be it

text_fidelity_a:
WindTook leisure backpack for Women College Book Bag Travel Work Daypack Laptop Computer Bag with USB Charging Port Suits 15 Inch Notebook,Cyan I have had the opportunity to test and review many different back / daypacks and have a good understanding of features and the difference between quality packs and those of lesser quality. This is a quality pack - that being said, this is more of a daypack rather than a travel or school backpack.

The outer shell is a heavy duty canvas material that is definitely made to hold up to wear and tear. I love the outer black and grey color scheme.

The outer most pocket has a zippered pocket (5” x 8”) on the very front and unbuttons at the top to access the full size front pocket (9” x 11”).

Both sides of the bag have snap closed pockets which could carry water bottles or umbrellas. In addition the right side has an exterior USB charging port.

The top of the bag has a double zipper closure that is then covered by a heavy canvas flap that snaps in place via snaps located on the front of the bag. This double sealing system is excellent for both security and waterproofing.

The interior of the primary compartment is HUGE. The lid itself has a zippered mesh pocket for storing items you may need easy access too.

When looking down into the primary compartment, on the left you’ll see the USB cable that leads to the exterior charging port on the right exterior of the bag - this is meant to be plugged into a power supply that then can be stored in the first pouch pocket on the upper interior side of this compartment. Following this pouch there are two smaller, pen sized pouches and then another larger one capable of holding a phone. Above these four pouches is a zippered pocket (7” x 9”). The bottom and rear side of this compartment are heavily padded with the rear wall having double storage specifically for a laptop and tablet. There is a Velcro closure strap that holds your electrics securely in place. The laptop storage area is 10” x 17” while the pocket on the front of that area is 8” x 9” - I was able to squeeze my 17” laptop into the laptop sleeve and Velcro it securely in place and feel like it was adequately protected.

In regards to the shoulder straps, they have a breathable material where they rest against your shoulders which help keep it cooler when carrying. The back is padded and I found the bag comfortable to carry when fully loaded. Above the shoulder straps is a vinyl covered handle that is a bit small for this size bag but is attached well.

All of the snaps, seams and zippers are attached very well - craftsmanship is superb.

While I love the exterior color scheme of this bag, in the bag I received the liner is a bright teal color - obviously this is a personal preference, but I believe it would look much more professional in a royal or navy blue.

This is a great bag for carrying as a daypack - such as to the beach or for an overnight trip. Due to it not being able to unzip and open flat for TSA screening I would not advise it for traveling and it lacks the multiple good sized pockets students require in order to keep their books, notebooks and school supplies organized and easy to find.

This is a well constructed bag that looks nice and is made to hold up. I would certainly recommend it for the purposes I mentioned.

Mohu Sky 60 TV Antenna, Outdoor, Amplified, 75 Mile Range, Durable Lightweight, Mount Kit Included, Roof or Attic, 4K-Ready, 30 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, MH-110585,Black REVISED to 4 Star review: After using the antenna a week, I re-ran the channel search--which I should have done after installing it. I am able to pick up 38 of the 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my house. They all come in very clearly. The amplifier wasn't working at all, and we determined that the brick was defective. Plugging it into another USB brick didn't really improve the signal by much, but it at least worked.

All-in-all, I'm glad I bought it. I'm able to clearly receive: 4 PBS stations; 3 CBS stations; 1 each NBC and ABC; plus FOX, CW, and an assortment of crap (TCT, HSN, QVC) networks. Enough to make me happy to leave TWC and in the dust.

UPDATE: 8/2/2016 What I have found is that the signals from channels with transmitters within 10 miles are not being up, while those 12 miles and beyond are coming in clearly. I suspect this is due to my location and not the antenna. Still, the amplifier causes the entire thing to not work, so I don't know what's up with that thing.

This antenna arrived as indicated. However, instead of the nearly 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my home, I'm only able to get about 15. I installed it on the roof, and the direction did not seem to make a difference. NOTES:

Originally, I hooked this up and leaned it against the back of the TV before I had someone install it. I got no more channels installing it on the roof than I did that way.

The amplifier which comes in the box with this antenna actually made the signal worse--not better, so I disconnected that.

Give the few number of channels that actually come through, on hindsight, I would have bought a much cheaper antenna. It does not pull in channels more than about 20 miles away. Even channels 20 miles away aren't received.

Otherwise, the reception on the channels that do come through is great.

All of this may be because I am in an old, downtown neighborhood, with close houses and lots of trees. Although I installed it in an area of the roof free of trees.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones I use headphones very frequently under a number of different environments including noisy computer labs, airplanes, quiet rooms and more. I am particularly familiar with noise canceling phones but I do have a some non-ANC phones that I use for listening to music in quiet environments. This pair of Amazon Basics headphones is my least expensive pair but it actually compares reasonably well against some more expensive phones.

First, the Basics headphones are very lightweight on-ear phones. They are slightly tight though not so tight to cause discomfort. What they do cause for me is a bit of warmth on the ears, something that I have not experienced very often when using headphones. It’s a minor aggravation, not a show-stopper by any means.

The most important feature of any headphones is the sound profile. I like electronic music which has a wide range of sound frequency - abundant highs, full midrange and quite a bit of bass. When listening to tracks with these phones, the first thing that I could not help but notice is that they overdrive the bass a little much, but this seems to be more the norm with headphones anymore. The highs sound just about right - not exceptionally sharp but not muted either. The midrange, though, is off and reminds me of listening to music in a tunnel. It isn’t terrible, but it’s noticeable. From what I can tell, the bass is so overdriven that it partially flattens the midrange.

I compared these headphones to a pair of Munitio PRO40 phones, a much more expensive set ($350 full retail) of phones that I use for studio work. Yes, the Munitio phones outperformed the Basics phones, but the difference did not match the $300 price difference. Other than the midrange, the Basics phones compared very well on the sound spectrum. That’s more than I could have asked for at $15.

If this was an expensive set of phones I would be very upset. However, this is a VERY inexpensive set and for the price range sounds much better than average.

Construction-wise this set of phones feels well-made. They won’t hold up to abuse, but with proper care they should last a long time. They even come with a cloth carry bag with offers little more than scratch protection but it’s a nice touch.

Considering how inexpensive these headphones are, I am hard-pressed to criticize. In their price range they are well above average in terms of sound and construction. If you are looking for a lightweight and inexpensive set of headphones and you do not need the very best in sound this is an outstanding value.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones

Nikon AF-S Nikkor 50mm f/1.8G Lens I bought this lens to do portraits and general low-light photography, and don't regret it for a minute. It looks a little stunted on the Nikon D7000 after taking off the telephoto, but is a dream to carry around and a snap to use.

Paired with the [[ASIN:B001BTG3OQ Nikon SB-900 AF Speedlight Flash for Nikon Digital SLR Cameras]], anyone can take a picture perfect portrait, and you can capture gorgeous bokeh and snap away in low light situations thanks to the large 1.8 aperture. For the beginner, this lens can autofocus, but you can also switch to manual if preferred. As it is a prime lens, you have to move around to compose your shots (no lazy zooming in) but if you want full body shots, you'll have to move back quite a bit so as not to cut off heads or feet. Same goes for group shots - this isn't an ideal lens for large groups of people.

Verbatim 32GB Store 'n' Flip USB Flash Drive - Violet, 0.3 x 0.8 x 2.2 I have had good fortune with Verbatim products in the past, particularly blank CDs. I was excited to try this thumb drive and it has worked out well for me so far. The biggest plus is the size of the whole unit.

This is a 32GB drive which is a good size for most things anymore. It is good as a mass storage device but it also is suitable as boot media if you need to use it for recovery media, OS replacement or other things. There are bigger thumbs drives out there, but this one is big enough for most.

It comes preformatted with a FAT32 file system which makes it easy to read by practically all modern operating systems. My Linux system is able to mount it and read it, and Windows 10 opens it automatically. I likely will reformat it though for a better-performing file system to use primarily on my Linux system.

I looked on the drive for hidden files and found only the system volume stuff.

I did not make notes on the read/write speeds but it seems to perform on par with other name-brand drives I have. I have worked with drives that are quite slow when copying larger files like ISO images; this one seems about average when compared to Sandisk and PNY drives.

Where this drive really distinguishes itself, though, is in the very small size, which is good but also could be a problem. It folds up to about the size of a nickel (approximately) and easily fits in a change pocket. This keeps it out of the way and makes it easy to toss in a bag, purse, pocket or backpack even when it’s full. However, it also means it can easily find its way into the laundry.

So far, I have no complaints with this drive and am happy to recommend it. It performs well, it is easily recognized on different platforms and is small enough to go just about anywhere.
text_fidelity_b: Verbatim 32GB Store 'n' Flip USB Flash Drive - Violet, 0.3 x 0.8 x 2.2

ViewTV Digital TV Converter Box for Analog TV - AT-163 OTA DVR, PVR Digital TV Recorder and ATSC Tuner Features A Built in USB Port, HDMI and Coaxial Output, Bright LED Clock and is Easy to Use First I want to say that the first box I received did not work correctly immediately. The box kept failing to maintain recognition that my external drives were in fact present, no matter how many different types I used. There was surely something wrong with the ViewTV. (The ViewTV I received had software version installed from last month.)

I called the ViewTV company and they were really great. The nice tech support guy agreed I had to have something wrong with the unit...and he rushed me out a replacement. The replacement works much better...and interestingly its software version is dated 7 months ago.

I think the ViewTV at $50 is really a great value. (And I was impressed with the customer service the company provided.)

Running the antenna channel scan is relatively fast. The picture quality on my replacement box is stellar. Moving through all the settings menus is very easy and straightforward. Everything is easy to figure out.

When you think about the box's limitations, as pointed out by some very helpful reviews here, you must keep in mind the very reasonable price.

For $50 you get a good over the air box with a good tuner that sends a great picture via HDMI to your TV. You can time shift your viewing, if you plug in a drive to the USB port, and you can record programs to said drive.

For $50 you cannot expect multiple tuners or a great TV Guide. But at least you get to see the very basic guide info the broadcasters send down with their OTA signal. (My two HDTV's on their own do not show the OTA program info, which is very disappointing.)

For cable cutters out there on a budget, this box is definitely something you should consider. It delivers really well exactly what it promises.
text_fidelity_b: ViewTV Digital TV Converter Box for Analog TV - AT-163 OTA DVR, PVR Digital TV Recorder and ATSC Tuner Features A Built in USB Port, HDMI and Coaxial Output, Bright LED Clock and is Easy to Use

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device

text_fidelity_a:
OhO Audio Sunglasses,Open Ear Audio Sunglasses Speaker to Listen Music and Make Phone Calls,Water Resistance and Full UV Lens Protection for Outdoor Sports and Compatiable for All Smart Phones Let's get one thing straight right away: THESE ARE NOT SUNGLASSES. They are blue-light blocking at best, or just mildly tinted most likely. I took them out of the box and thought "Oh cool! These are the kinds of glasses that get dark outside and transparent when you are inside!", but nope- I wore them for a full hour outside and they didn't get any darker or exhibit any sun blocking properties AT ALL. So that's false advertising right there. They aren't for use in the sun. They don't darken anything.
As far as audio quality... they are a cool concept, but again, falls short of expectations. The open ear design means the speakers have to work harder to be audible. That means they often make those tin-sounding rattles that tiny speakers make when cranked up too high. This is definitely NOT cool for music as most of the fidelity is lost right off the bat, and adding insult to injury is that they often don't get loud enough to use outside. I'm not saying using it in a crowded subway terminal (that you can just forget about completely), I'm talking about even just going for a stroll around my suburban block with some birds chirping and the wind blowing lightly, maybe a car driving in the distance. I tried listening to a recorded lecture (since music was a lost cause), and they couldn't get loud enough to hear clearly. The microphone for calls was OK in my test, so I guess they are cool as a way to take a phone call without wearing a headset, but that only works if you're wearing these anyway as sunglasses. They aren't sunglasses, so you wouldn't be wearing them anyway, and you wouldn't be wearing them for music, and you wouldn't be wearing them to make a phone call either because they rarely get loud enough unless you are home alone... in which case you can put your phone on speaker and avoid this whole mess.
In conclusion- its a good idea but executed poorly and does NOT live up to expectations. I'm surprised there are so many good reviews on this product. I can't think of a time I would use it.
text_fidelity_b: OhO Audio Sunglasses,Open Ear Audio Sunglasses Speaker to Listen Music and Make Phone Calls,Water Resistance and Full UV Lens Protection for Outdoor Sports and Compatiable for All Smart Phones

This product is so easy to install and works perfectly! The length of the cords is pretty much perfect, so I can station my two towers well away from each other and thus avoid heat buildup, which could happen if they had to be positioned too close to one another.

I would suggest only one or two small improvements to make this setup work even better. I would label the switch itself with A/B tags, and I would also put two, different colored LED lights on each end of the switcher, which would each light up, depending on which computer one is working on. That way, the user can quickly visually identify which computer is currently in use, instead of trying to guess.

I have put A/B tags on my switcher and on my respective computers too. However, since the switch is not a toggle switch, I often still have to figure out which computer I am working from when I don't remember where I left off the time before.

Otherwise, this device seems to perform seamlessly. Just remember that when you are rebooting one of the computers, be sure to keep the peripherals connected until they are recognized. Otherwise, when you toggle back again, you may find a screen with very large graphics on it - like I did once. I just had to reboot and stay with that computer until I saw the Windows welcome screen. After that all went fine.

I have a Windows 7 computer and an XP connected to this. My peripherals are HP w2007 Monitor, Altec Lansing VS2521 2.1 Powered Speaker System, Microsoft Natural Ergonomic Keyboard 4000 v1.0 (USB) and a Logitech Cordless Trackman Wheel (USB). Have not yet tried my Logitech USB Desktop Microphone.

Great product at a very nice price. I recommend it highly!

NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming I have been using NETGEAR products for many years and am quite familiar with how they work and their quirks.

The fact that this unit has a built in Ethernet port is what led me to wanting this WiFi extender - the smart TV which is farthest from the primary router has had difficulty maintaining a solid connection so I wanted to utilize the Ethernet port on this extender to plug my TV directly into.

Set up of the extender was fairly straightforward, I plugged it into a power supply and ran an Ethernet cable from it to my laptop. The NETGEAR EXTENDER setup program auto loaded and was easy to follow. I setup the router to keep my same network name and password, it saved all of the information to my extender without issue. I unplugged the extender from both the power supply and my computer and located it into the bedroom, plugged it in and it found and connected to my WiFi without any issue. I plugged the smart TV into the Ethernet port and it connected beautifully - loading Netflix, HULU and Amazon Prime lightning fast.

The only hiccup happened when I finished that as the rest of my network went haywire with my smart devices not connecting and reconnecting. I restarted my modem and my primary router and everything appears to be back to operating as normal. I’m not sure what caused the glitch.

I can definitely see a WiFi speed increase in the area of the house that the extender is located and the TV that is plugged into the Ethernet port is streaming perfectly.

I am very pleased with this extender and would recommend it to anyone who needed to extend their WiFi range or provide an Ethernet Port to a device that is too far from their current hub.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming

text_fidelity_a:
JOBY UltraFit Sling Strap for Women Horribly Uncomfortable.

What's the one thing that makes a good neck strap comfortable for long term wearing? Padding. What's the one thing this strap is completely lacking? Padding!

The part of the strap that's supposed to go around your neck is a two inch wide very rough textured bit of nylon webbing. Seat belts are softer than this material. The first time I tried the Joby UltraFit Sling Strap I carried my Kodak Z990 around for about an hour and it was so uncomfortable. Who designs a neck strap with NO padding?

This strap attaches to your camera via the ¼" tripod screw mount on the bottom of the camera. It's odd that your camera hangs upside down and I don't like the single point of failure mounting. Also, because of the way it's designed it puts angular force on the mounting threads when hanging and even more when releasing or engaging the quick release latch. Since the threads in my Kodak are plastic I have even more dislike for this mounting system. Additionally, you have to dismount your strap any time you want to use a tripod or monopod.

I found in the time I used this that the only time the (non) padded portion of the strap is on your neck is when the rig is retracted when you use the 'Speed Cinch' to bring the camera up for shooting, at least on my extra large frame, the whole strap rotates forward and puts the even more uncomfortable thinner strap around your neck and the 'padded' section down on your chest.

To sum it up... it's uncomfortable. It completely lacks any padding. It has an odd mounting system that puts lever like force on your tripod socket and you have to take the strap off to use a tripod or monopod. The only good point to this system is that it is rather well made. Unfortunately it's just well made junk. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone for any application.
text_fidelity_b: JOBY UltraFit Sling Strap for Women

These sometimes leave residue behind, so I was interested in trying this electric duster to see if it would cut down on residue and save money in the long run. I will confess that I was not very optimistic and thought it would be underpowered. However, it has proven to be as effective as a canned duster in cleaning keyboards and other equipment, without leaving any residue and without losing power like canned dusters tend to do as they get cold.

This device is smaller than a tea kettle and relatively light. It requires an AC outlet so it does need to be plugged in when you want to use it. I was hopeful I had missed something on the description and that there was a rechargeable battery but unfortunately this is not the case. This was me being hopeful, not a confusing write-up.

It comes with a few attachments to help direct the air flow over the surface of what you’re trying to clean. The most helpful attachment, to me, is the round nozzle, but all of them have their uses.

I took it to my office where we have an abundance of dirty keyboards that need to be cleaned, and I set to work. I was expecting it to do a mediocre cleaning job, but it gave me a very pleasant surprise and blew air with plenty of force to clean out the clumps of dust that collect under the keys. More importantly, though, the power didn’t diminish like what tends to happen with canned dusters as they get cold, and there was no problem with frost buildup either.

So far, this is proving to be a useful and helpful tool. It produces enough force to get the job done without losing power, and it leaves no residue behind.

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP

It installed somewhat easily and except for a little problem with the wireless PC card for the laptop (wouldn't be recognized at first but easily corrected) we had pretty stable use for about a year. Powering down and restarting the router, modem and computer seemed to correct the issue. But as of this morning the router appears to have completely died. Powering down and restarting does nothing, the internet connection cannot be re-established. We can connect the desktop directly to the cable modem but for now the laptop is without connection, making for some unhappy family members here.

As of right now I don't know if we'll be buying another Netgear router & wireless PC card. The life expectancy of Netgear products does not appear to be all that great. Looking at some of the reviews we appear to be quite lucky that we got as much time out of the router as we did. Still I'm not in the mood to be shopping for a new router every 1.5 years or less. Hopefully there is a good router out there that can last at least two years.

Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music.

If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

That card had followed me from a Note II to a Note 3 to my current Note 4. I was a little concerned about compatibility and reliability because a few years ago tried to save a buck by getting a tier 2 brand card that literally melted down.

This time I took a chance with this non-Samsung card and cannot be more pleased. For one thing, the transfer from my old card to this one did not cause this to get hot. Considering that there was about 29GB involved that was my first indication that this is a well made card.

Another thing is after I transferred the contents to this card (via a card reader), as soon as I popped it into my Note 4, it immediately mounted and everything on the older card was there. I took the time to look for corrupted files, sampled a lot of random music, and checked a few videos. Zero issues and the Note 4 did not balk at this card or any of the files on it.

As for speed, I am not going to make claims one way or the other. I did not test it with benchmarking software, and since I use this mainly for streaming music the additional speed (if any) is not noticeable anyway. What is noticeable is the total compatibility with my Note 4 and the extra breathing room the capacity provides me.

Overall I am not only pleased, I feel as though this card is a better value than the Samsung brand cards that I had been purchasing. And every bit as reliable too.

Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI) This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. The signal indicator light is easy to read and is quite bright. Since the device is in our hallway, it acts as a nice night light and would be rather distracting if it were in a bedroom.

The end result: the dead spots are gone. We can use all of our devices in the those areas without having to worry about losing a signal.

Fujifilm Instax Mini Link Smartphone Printer - Beige Gold We have had Polaroid cameras in the past when they resurrected them for a while, and they were okay, but you wasted a lot of pictures that did not turn out too great. Let's take a look at this.

WHAT IS THIS SMARTPHONE PRINTER LIKE?
This printer is really handy. It is small, easy to carry, recharges well, and is easy to work. It comes with a USB charging cord, instruction book, and a small roll of paper/film. 10 is the number that came with the one I got.

WHAT IS THE ADVANTAGE OF THIS PRINTER?
Although this is a similar idea to the old Polaroid cameras, the difference with this one is that you get to choose the pictures that you want to print, instead of having to print whatever you take.

DOES IT WORK WELL?
This printer worked great. It is not hard at all to print with and we had no trouble with it.

INSTRUCTION BOOK
The instruction book is easy to follow and use.

QUALITY OF PHOTOS
I am enclosing a photo we took and printed with this printer. It is small and easy to keep handy, but still a great photo to put in a tiny frame as a magnet on the refrigerator, or framed for a small desk area. There are plenty of other things we can do with it, but those are just a few ideas.

WHAT DID WE USE IT FOR?
Our kids went to a pretty big march/event not too long ago and they were able to take a quick photo of them and their friends and print everyone a small copy as a memory to hang on to (especially since 1 of them was not too into tech stuff).

IS IT WORTH IT?
The replacement paper is not cheap, but it is doable if you make sure to keep it handy and only use it for special photos. This only comes with 10 so it is easy to blow through that in one sitting. It is nice to have handy, but only if you use it wisely.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a good quality instant print photo to help quickly capture a photo you take with your phone in print, this is a nice little printer. It is easy to carry and store, but it does take expense to keep printer paper handy.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS although it is more like four and a half. I would think this would come with a bit more paper to get you started with it, but not enough of a pain to take a star off at this point.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Mini Link Smartphone Printer - Beige Gold

Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation) The Flip is a pint-sized camcorder with a surprising feature set given its compactness. Though is it not a full-featured camcorder and I would not recommend it for serious recording (special events or production material), it is excellent for on-the-go shots and for spontaneous recording when opportunities present themselves.

The Flip is small - a little smaller than an ice cream sandwich. It may be little, but there's tremendous convenience in being able to drop your camcorder in your shirt pocket or your purse and have it at the ready. This compact size holds everything you need to start recording - batteries, flash RAM and all. Without tapes or DVD media on which to record, there's little reason for this device to be any bigger.

It is a solid little thing and feels durable. That doesn't mean it would do well if dropped or stepped on, but it likely will be ok if jostled a little.

Recording is simple. No, I should be more clear - recording with the Flip is trivial. There is no real science to using it: turn it on, point and press record. Press the record button again to stop recording. Even technological novices, or people afraid of electronics will have no trouble using the Flip to record. Playing back is equally simple - once the recording is finished, press the Play button.

There are + and - buttons, used for Zoom. The Flip doesn't have a particularly capable zoom, so shooting from a distance will not yield especially great results.

I tested this camcorder in my basement on a bright, sunny day, and I wandered about recording and chattering to myself. When I played back what I had recorded, I made a pleasant discovery - it does some light balancing and deals with changes in light levels so that the video is still clear. The sound is also good, better than I expected. When I walked down a dark hallway and into an unlit room, it had tried very hard to accommodate for the lack of light but it was unable to completely overcome the darkness. As there is no light on the camcorder to come on when it is dark, this is understandable, but it did surprisingly well in spite of that.

I attached the Flip to my computer to pull the video to my hard drive. FlipShare installed itself and started up, seeing the video I had made. It allowed me to pull it over and even gave me the option to delete it from the camera. Once finished, I was able to play the video through FlipShare. Instead, I decided to hunt it down and use a different application to play it.

I found the file and tried to open it with Windows Media Player. I got audio, but not video. When I switched to QuickTime, my video came up and filled my screen. This is the point at which I made an unfortunate discovery. Every minute move I had made while recording was now plainly obvious, as there is no anti-jitter built into the device.

The video, on a 1440x900 resolution screen, looked clear. It records at 1280x720, which is not that much smaller, so I was a little surprised. I would have expected a little pixelation, but this actually was not an issue.

There are few settings that can be adjusted on the Flip - language, date, time and recording light.

The Flip is a nice camcorder that provides tremendous convenience and fun. It is very easy to use and very compact. It is important to remember that it has some limitations which make it a less-than-ideal choice for more serious application, but if those limitations are not an issue for you then the Flip is a fun and affordable way to capture things on video.
text_fidelity_b: Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation)

SAFEMORE USB Power Strip 8-Outlet and 4 USB Charging Ports with 6.5-Feet Cord (Pure Black) I have a workbench where I frequently have little projects underway, and the issue I have had is a shortage of power outlets so I am frequently changing the configuration on my desk to account for this. I decided to use this surge suppressor/power strip on my workbench to resolve this issue and so far it has worked out well for me.

There are eight full-sized, grounded power outlets on this tower, and each one is spaced properly to handle a full-sized power adapter like what comes with many electronics. As such, there is no need to compromise when plugging in devices that have larger adapters, because there is enough room for all on this tower. Every outlet includes a ground plug too, which is great for devices that require one (in my house, it's about 50/50). With almost every other surge suppressor, I have had issues with oversized adapters crowding other outlets – this is not a problem with this one.

There are also four USB charging ports on this tower which is a really nice bonus. These are all 2.1A ports so they can output a full-speed charge to devices that can handle it, but most of my devices take a 1A charge so the 2.1A is lost on me. I have not yet put a meter on these ports to check the actual power output but so far these seem to output about the same as most other USB charging blocks I have used. Power output aside, having USB and AC ports together allows choice if you have a device that uses a USB adapter to plug into an AC outlet.

The circuit breaker button is on the bottom.

One thing I particularly like about this tower is that the outlets are one two circuits and there are buttons (on the top) that control each circuit. This may require a little logic when planning your power usage – if you want only/all lights on one circuit, place them so that they are controlled by a single button and you can then power them all on and off together.

This tower have allowed me to clean up my work area and it has enough outlets on it to cover my devices without issue. It is very easy to use and understand, it has plenty of outlets that are spaced apart nicely so there is no waste, and it includes USB outlets too. I have had no trouble with it at all and have no problem recommending it it if you are looking for a good power strip/surge suppressor.

Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no/minimal cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black First a caveat: I am not of the generation who grew up carrying backpacks to school and I do not have a lot of shoulder/upper arm strength; in addition I have arthritis in my neck, so to me any backpack seems a bit strange, stiff, and awkward. Frankly, I think if I'd had to carry around all the books I did in junior high school in a backpack (none of my classes were near my homeroom locker, so there was none of this dropping books off routine--we only had three minutes to get between classes), I'd have severe back problems right now, remembering the thick English, math, science, Italian, and history textbooks, plus a full size ring binder. Oy.

Now to our backpack: I like this. We have less expensive backpacks in our home, to use as a "bug out" bag in case of emergency. This is much nicer: padding, quality of material, and lots of nice pockets (I am a pockets-type person). I particularly like the "hidden pocket" that faces your back, which would be useful for money or any other valuables if you were backpacking or traveling. I have preliminarily tested this by putting my laptop and my 10-inch tablet in the space provided and walking around for a bit. My laptop is six years old and weighs a ton. However, the padded shoulder straps and the sternum strap were helpful in keeping this balanced well on my back. I went up and down stairs a few times and did not feel unbalanced or "top heavy." (I do now, however, understand why people like Airbooks.)

In addition to the laptop pocket with the inner sleeve for the tablet, this has a central compartment with two pockets, one zipped, and an outside compartment with all sorts of slots for pens, memory cards, CDs, whatever. A small pocket on the top of the back could hold a cell phone or perhaps your printout of a boarding pass, parking ticket receipt, whatever, and there are two small pockets, one on each side, one with an opening so you could put an .mp3 player in the pocket and have your earbuds come out through it. This is all in addition to the "hidden pocket." There is a strong handle at either end of the backpack as well as a handle.

My goal is to give this a better workout at Dragoncon, where I can carry lunch and snacks and juice boxes in the central compartment, carry my tablet in the laptop compartment, and also carry my camera, instead of slinging a lunchbox and my camera case over my shoulder. It seems like a much better option. I also see it being useful on the occasional weekend trip. If it works out for me, it's possible my husband might enjoy one as well.

[September: This was really, really good at Dragoncon; I will be using a backpack again next year. Much better than carrying the lunchbox and the camera separately and wearing a pouch. I put my tablet in the laptop pocket, my lunch things (juice boxes, sandwiches, snacks, fruit) in the middle pocket, and the camera in the outermost pocket. The little pocket at the top held my spare cell phone batteries, and my wallet was in the hidden pocket. This backpack needs a strap at the bottom, and, instead of an iPod holder, a water bottle holder. That's the only thing I can see wrong with it. Yeah, I could have put a water bottle inside with my lunch.]

[PS I liked this so much I bought my husband one for Christmas.]
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black

text_fidelity_a:
PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV If you read the product description carefully, you won't waste time (as I did) trying to use this PLAYSTATION 4 UNIVERSAL MEDIA REMOTE to navigate PS4 games (e.g., Journey, Minecraft). The PS4 remote uses Bluetooth to turn your PS4 on and off, and to control and navigate PS4 media (e.g., DVDs), but only controls PS4 media. The PS4 remote can also be programmed to turn your TV, Cable Box, and Audio Receiver on and off, and to control and navigate those devices (assuming they accept remote Bluetooth operation).

The PS4 remote performs the advertised functions very well, and I'm happy with it. The main thing I wanted was the PS4 on/off feature, so that I wouldn't have to fool with the skinny button on the PS4 box when I wanted to play a DVD. But I also wanted something that would make it easier to navigate DVDs. I'm not much of a gamer, and I find the game controllers awkward to use. With the PS4 remote, the forward, back, play, and arrow buttons work "normally" (like any TV remote).

NOTE THAT once the PS4 remote is paired, you will turn the playstation "on" by pressing the big PS4 button, but you will turn it "off" by navigating to the PS4's power settings (in the display). (The PS4 remote doesn't have a "sources" button for bringing up the output options on my Samsung Smart TV, so I still need a second remote for selecting the PS4 output.)

The Bluetooth pairing and setup for the PS4 remote is straightforward, but you need to follow the directions in the accompanying booklet "to the letter". You have to visit several locations in the PS4 settings to add the remote to the PS4 device list, and then complete the setup.

Programming the remote to turn on another device (TV, Cable Box, Amplifier, etc.) is exactly the same as programming any universal remote. You turn on the device you're programming, put the remote into learning mode, point it at the device, and wait for the remote to find, recognize, and turn off the device. If the remote doesn't recognize the device, you must perform the device code programming manually (lots of codes are listed in the instruction booklet). The PS4 remote recognized my TV without difficulty, but my sound bar required manual programming.
