text_fidelity_a:
B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography I am best described as a skilled amateur when it comes to photography and I am always looking for ways to get better and to build my knowledge and ability. I am not a professional by any means, but I know a lot more than the average selfie-taker. I have wanted a ring light for a little while and I was delighted to have the chance to get to use this one. It does work, in the right circumstances, but it is definitely aimed at the base consumer market and is priced accordingly.

Thought it can be used as part of a professional set-up, it is designed and marketed as a consumer-grade unit. There are a number of obvious design decisions that make this more than just a little apparent. The tripod is good, but the mounts are designed for smartphones and will not work for DSLR cameras, mirrorless cameras or video cameras. That’s ok, as it is clearly marketed that way. The unit uses a USB power source which is an important point – the light itself isn’t especially bright like one that uses a normal AC power source. To be effective, the light needs to be fairly close to the subject. If a dim directional light is needed, a regular desk lamp is more than adequate in most cases. The upshot is that using USB power makes it much more portable for travel (more on that in a moment).

The remote allows for making a few adjustments to the light itself. There are three color modes and ten brightness modes, all of which can be (rather, must be) set through the remote. The adjustments are sufficient for this grade of light, though I would have found more colors and a more smooth graduation in brightness to be more useful. That’s more of a nitpick than a criticism considering the price point.

Build-wise, this unit is acceptable. It should hold up well enough in the studio or home office. What is lacking is a carry case to protect it when travelling. Considering the target audience (social media producers), this is an oversight that I think is important. To transport this light, it should be well secured and the only recourse as sold is to put it back in the original box, and that’s just unwieldy. Plan accordingly if you choose to transport this light.

This is an adequate unit for its target audience but will leave the aspiring professional underwhelmed. If you are looking for something that will work sufficiently for making posts to social media this is a reasonable unit; if you need a serious ring light for photography, consider other options. The main problem with this light is the fact that it is designed for portability but comes with no carrying case; keep this in mind.
text_fidelity_b: B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography

Targus Versavu Rotating Keyboard Case and Stand for iPad 2, 3, and 4, Black (THZ17101US) This polyurethane Targus Versavu Keyboard Case is beautiful, with imitation-leather exterior and suede-like "soft touch" interior. A hard shell (also with imitation-leather exterior) holds the iPad firmly in place, yet the iPad can be easily removed. The shell is attached at the circular hole shown in the product photos; the hole allows the Apple logo to show through. The shell rotates (with the iPad inserted) a full 360 degrees, so that the stand and keyboard can be used when the iPad is oriented either horizontally or vertically.

The lightweight keyboard is about the same size as the keyboard on my Toshiba netbook. The flat, non-contoured keys are reasonably comfortable to use. The keyboard is surrounded by a raised edge, to prevent scratches or damage to the iPad screen. The keyboard must be charged independently (using the included USB cable, attached to your computer). The keyboard will give a low-charge warning at 15% power, and shut down at 10% power.

This case (with cutouts for buttons, switches, rear camera, and charger plug) fits my iPad 2 perfectly, and the Bluetooth keyboard connects with my iPad 2. I didn't expect it to work, because the iPad 2 is equipped with Bluetooth 2.1 + EDR technology, while the iPad 3 is equipped with Bluetooth 4.0 technology, and the product description says that the case requires an iPad 3. The case does NOT have an automatic iPad Wake/Sleep switch that operates when you open the cover; however, the keyboard puts itself to sleep after 10 minutes of inactivity.

I like this case and all of its features, but it's not the "perfect" iPad 2 case. It adds weight and bulk, and apparently--judging from other reviewers' statements--the manufacturer recommends against using the case for anything but display (no carrying the case around in a backpack, tote, or bag). Because the keyboard works well, I rate it at 3.5 stars, rounded up to 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Versavu Rotating Keyboard Case and Stand for iPad 2, 3, and 4, Black (THZ17101US)

Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue *UPDATED REVIEW*

A seller replaced a different defective FM transmitter unit with this one for me (mine has the Kollea brand name on it, but this is the identical unit, private-labeled). This is a better product than what it replaced, but is not without it's flaws. I have three (*UPDATE: now four, and the fourth one is a deal-breaker--see below) complaints with this unit:

1) It will not automatically reconnect to my phone about 75% of the time. I have to manually shut Bluetooth off and turn it back on on the phone, sometimes a few times before it pairs successfully. This is a hassle--a PITA. Every time I get in the car, I have to go through this process--every time power is cut from the transmitter, actually, so if your passenger knocks it and it pops out of the 12V socket, it will have to be re-paired, which is supposed to happen automatically, but does not, and you then have to go through the process. Frustrating.

2) Charge output is only 1.0A. this is why I returned the first one--phone gives a "slow charging" warning when charging from this unit, regardless of what USB cable I use (I tried four different cables, all of which I know for certain can carry 2.1A).

3) Callers have occasionally complained they cannot hear me well when using this unit, and I occasionally (but not often) encounter FM interference. I believe Bluetooth itself is part of the problem, and anyone who has used a few Bluetooth headsets or units like this knows audio quality is terrible. Period. We just deal with it. Add to that the burden of having to transmit your signal via FM to a car stereo and the user-side audio (what you will hear in your car) is always going to be craptastic.

4) (*UPDATE) When paired, voice recognition on my phone, which is usually quite good, becomes severely impaired. This is also likely the culprit for complaint #3, above. I suspect this is because when paired, it tries to use the built-in microphone for voice recognition instead of the microphones on my phone (of which there are 4). It is disabling the extremely good microphones in my phone (Nokia lumia Icon which is well known for having incredible audio input) and using the unit's crappy microphone instead. This microphone is located in the unit, which is attached to the center console of my car near the shifter, and thus picks up all the vibrations and related road and engine noise transmitted through the structure of the car as I drive. This approach is terrible. I have stopped using the unit for anything requiring voice input, including telephone calls. In other words, this is just a big awkward charger now, and one that charges painfully slowly (see complaint #2). If it were possible to disable the onboard mic, and use the mics in my phone instead for calls and voice recognition, this would be a much more serviceable unit As it is now, it is just a piece of junk.

Cannot recommend this item. There are definitely worse products out there. I have not tried them all, but of those I have used, this is the best one so far. I will likely keep using it until the lack of automatic pairing pushes me over the edge with it one day and I get something else. (*UPDATE: this thing just does not work well, and I am now looking for something else.)
text_fidelity_b: Nulaxy Bluetooth Car FM Transmitter Audio Adapter Receiver Wireless Handsfree Voltmeter Car Kit TF Card AUX 1.44 Display – KM18 Peacock Blue

text_fidelity_a:
WixGear Sport Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Over Ear Sport Headphones with Touch Control, and Charging Case Stereo Deep Bass Sound,30H Playtime Sweat-Proof Bluetooth Earphones with Mic For my uses, these are great. They were very well packaged and secure for shipping. The box is very nice and sturdy, lined with foam. I need to hear the environment around me. This has been an issue with previous earbuds. Commercials between videos or songs can get so loud! That is the deal-breaker for me, as it's a safety issue. These do not get too loud, even on the loudest setting, so I am able to remain safe. I don't have an issue hearing the sounds coming from the buds, but I'm not in high-traffic outdoor areas regularly either. My ear canals are unusually small for an adult. I was afraid these may be too-big, but they are snug. Any bigger and it may have been an issue. I used the smaller of the plastic tips. Over the ear designs are the only ones that have ever worked for me. I did look at some other models in the past, but I found them a bit more expensive than I felt justified to spend unknowing how well they may work for me. However, knowing how well these work, I find them to be a really great value and would have purchased them before if I had known how well they worked. It was only by chance they were up for review and I had been seeking a replacement on my old pair that I've been using for the past few years.

The Bluetooth is nice. I have a simple cell phone. It only took asking my phone to connect to work. It was the easiest that I have ever had with connecting anything Bluetooth to my phone. I liked this as I'm not the most savvy at using Bluetooth electronics. If I can do it, anyone can.

I'm not great at using the buttons as they are really sensors on the flat-side of the body on the earbuds. I'm getting used to it but they are touch sensitive and there is a correct spot and amount of pressure that works best. I'm still getting a feel for it and there is a slight delay, so it's very easy to double-tap. The included booklet has been helpful to learn to use these straight out of the package.

Sometimes I get down on the floor at the gym to use the foam rollers and stretches, other times I'm using them in the car to take calls. I've tried them at work as well. Every scenario has worked well for me. I really do wish I've had these before. Sometimes while getting my breaks at work, I would want to listen to things from my phone, but didn't want to risk disturbing my co-workers with some of the news and hobby related videos I enjoy. I asked a few co-workers if they could hear my earbud noise, they could not.

The case is very easy to use as well and fits easily into my pockets. I'm a lady, so my pockets are not always very generously sized. It charges very quickly, and I've not found myself running out of charge. I cannot speak on the long-term durability for this as they are new. If/when I experience any issues with the charge, I will be sure to post an update.

In summary, these would be better for users that need to hear their surroundings for safety. For those that want extreme high volume, they may not be as happy. They stay on my ears securely and the case works very well. I'm pleasantly surprised how well I like these and hope that they are durable since they are working so well for me.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.

NETGEAR Orbi Whole Home Tri-band Mesh WiFi 6 System (RBK752) – Router with 1 Satellite Extender | Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft., 40 Devices | AX4200 (Up to 4.2Gbps) This is the first mesh system I've used. I had a Linksys router and an Asus router before this, both installed with third-party firmware. After the Asus upgrade, I used the Linksys router as a repeater. The signal was okay; considering I had Xfinity 250Mbps, the Asus worked fantastically, while the Linksys trailed behind. We live in an old apartment building with thick, plaster walls, so signal can be very spotty.

With this mesh system, I saw a huge upgrade the first week. Setup was very easy; quick instructions are provided. As soon as the setup was complete, I delved into the firmware. I recall being a little disappointed as I was used to the Asus custom firmware (Asuswrt-Merlin). The Asus firmware "just werqed." I run a small server, and setup was super easy with the Asus. With the Netgear, it was a lot more involved. Setting up outside ports was a pain; at the time, there was no simple way of forwarding ports. I recall a little workaround I was able to conduct with the server, but it took me days to figure out.

The firmware also lacks time restrictions for devices (at least of this writing). Asuswrt-Merlin allows me to set specific times to shut off internet for devices, which comes in handy with a large family.

As for the actual mesh system, so far so good. I can't tell when I'm using the main router or the satellite. The devices connect automatically without hiccup. I've since ditched Xfinity in favor of RCN 1Gbps; this mesh system works very well with the service. Once we have fiber, I can't wait to see the results.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Whole Home Tri-band Mesh WiFi 6 System (RBK752) – Router with 1 Satellite Extender | Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft., 40 Devices | AX4200 (Up to 4.2Gbps)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S) howdy y'all,

i bought this mouse to replace my logitech mx1100 cordless mouse. that one finally had the left mouse button start doing the dreaded false double click. it lasted several years, so i was not seriously annoyed. [*grin*]

for those coming from an mx1100, here are differences i noticed ...
- the mx1100 had the hump in the center instead of towards the back, so the main mouse buttons were shorter
this makes the mouse seem really rather too long. i am unsure if that will bother me once i use the new one for a while.

- the mx1100 had less of a slant to the right so that my hand sat a bit closer to level
the new one is more comfy for my very right-handed self.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel projected a tad more
combined with the sharp slant, the new mouse wheel feels like it is tilted the wrong way. it isn't, but i keep finding my finger on the right edge of the wheel instead of directly on the wheel.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel had a more pronounced side-move feel
the new mouse is very subtle. i liked the distinct feel of the older one when it toggled the side-move "button" function of the mouse wheel. of course, i like clicky keyboards, too ... [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had the upper thumb buttons just below the upper left edge
the new mouse has them on a surface that slants very sharply down to the left from the left edge. it makes the reach to the forward/back buttons a tad less comfy. combine that with a taper on those two buttons and i have found myself looking to see where the darned buttons went. they are also a tad more to the front of the mouse.
these admittedly annoying things that will likely fade out of my attention with use.

- the mx1100 used two AA rechargeable batteries
the new mouse uses one. since i use a lot of battery powered devices, i have a battery charger and several spares on hand. that means i will likely not use the usb charging function very often. still, one AA is better than having to charge two! [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had a larger usb wireless adapter
the new one is quite tiny! it works well - i put it on the back of my system among the tangle of wires that connect to other things and have had no reception problems.

*****
the parts list says there otta be a driver cd included. _not_ so! [*sigh ...*] you are referred to their download site if you want to use any of the extended functions or buttons. the performance mx has a $100 recommended price and there is no excuse to cheap out like that. thankfully, win7x32 has basic mouse support for the standard buttons, the mouse wheel, and the back/forward buttons.

this is a /_serious_/ fubar and i almost subtracted a star from my rating because of it.
*****

i suspect that folks with short hands will have problems with this mouse, but i am getting used to it already. i'm 6'1" and my hand is 7.5" from base to middle finger tip. not a _large_ hand, but not short.

*****
rated a THREE since it does what i expected - no more and no less. still, i came very close to rating this a two for not including the cd.

take care,
lee
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Performance MX Wireless Mouse (DISCONTINUED and Replaced by MX Master 2S)

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) I've been using a Keurig machine for several years -- I currently own 2 of them. But I've always had an ethical issue with all the little plastic cups that get tossed into the environment. To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups.

I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups.

I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength.

As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem.

This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful.

I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning.

kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. Definitely comparable to the Ek​​​​obrew so far -- the only question I have is durability, and only time will tell. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review.
